  PROBLEM: The comment claims the body close-keyword matcher is "the same pattern _linked_prs_by_body_reference matches", but the two matchers are not the same: `_linked_prs_by_body_reference` (line 2902) uses `(?i)(close[sd]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[sd]?):?[[:space:]]+#<n>\b` with NO leading boundary, so a body containing "prefixes #77" or "hotfix #77" matches there, while the new predicate adds a leading `(^|[^[:alnum:]_-])` boundary and rejects those same bodies (pinned by the `("77", "claude/some-fix", "prefixes #77", 1)` test case).
  WHY: No runtime failure — the divergence is in the safe direction (the close-time predicate is strictly tighter than the enumeration helper, so it can only skip more, never close more). The defect is a misleading comment: a future maintainer editing one matcher to "restore parity" with the other could loosen the predicate and re-introduce the false-close class this PR fixes.
